subject: MAP: proposed re-prioritization and contingency for close date
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <s.liu@acmecorp.com>, Ben Jones <ben.jones@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-05T09:12:00Z
Subject: MAP: proposed re-prioritization and contingency for close date

Sarah / Ben —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Based on the procurement constraint you mentioned (legal needs extra review of the data residency clause) and the implementation team's availability next sprint, I sketched a short reprioritization so we can keep momentum and protect the current close window as much as possible. High level: 

- Target close (commercial signature): 2028-07-22 (unchanged target)
- Technical acceptance cutover: move from 2028-07-29 to 2028-08-05 (softening for procurement/infra lead time)
- Interim: phased pilot (read-only integration) to start 2028-07-25 — reduces go/no-go risk

Attached: rebaseline_matrix.xlsx (proposed milestone shifts), risk_log_v3.pdf (updated with procurement delay scenarios), map_timeline_v2.gsheet-link (live sheet).

Ask: can your legal team confirm whether the residency clause requires contractual redline vs appendix? If appendix is acceptable we can proceed with signature and add the residency appendix to the formal SOW post-signature — this preserves the close date while giving your legal negotiators runway.

Internal cc: Rishi / Laura / Connor — please review the attached risk log and the alternate cutover plan, and flag any operational blockers we should surface to the Acme execs if we accept the appendix route.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

Attachments: rebaseline_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), risk_log_v3.pdf (summary), map_timeline_v2.gsheet-link
From: Sarah Liu <s.liu@acmecorp.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Jones <ben.jones@acmecorp.com>, procurement@acmecorp.com
Date: 2028-07-05T14:03:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP: proposed re-prioritization and contingency for close date

Hannah —

Thanks for the clear note. Quick update from our side: legal has flagged the data residency language as material; their preferred path is to see the revised clause in the contract before we sign. They will not accept an appendix post-signature without senior legal approval. That adds an estimated 10 business days in our experience. Procurement is also pushing for a single signature step (commercial + technical acceptance together) to align budgets.

I understand the pilot approach helps the risk profile, but it doesn't move procurement/legal timelines. If Acme signs before legal gets its redline, it will slow our own internal approvals.

Is Redwood able to offer a temporary holdback (contract contingency) or an explicit SLA credit in case the appendix route fails? Procurement would entertain a signature if there's a short-term remediation path.

Thanks,
Sarah Liu
Head of IT Procurement — Acme Corp
s.liu@acmecorp.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Liu <s.liu@acmecorp.com>, Ben Jones <ben.jones@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2028-07-05T17:20:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP: proposed re-prioritization and contingency for close date

Hannah / team —

Reviewing Sarah's note and the attached risk log. Quick operational read and proposed mitigations: 

1) Appendix vs redline: materiality looks limited to the residency paragraph (data-at-rest location and logging retention). We can accept appendix for production environments if we formally encode a remediation path and an SLA credit tied to non-compliance. Legal will need to sign off on the credit formula but it's a smaller contract change than full clause replacement. 

2) Short-term commercial option: offer a 3% credit on first 6 months of usage tied to delivery milestones if appendix is rejected. This is defensible to finance for an enterprise concession and addresses procurement's desire for a commercial safety net.

3) Technical fallbacks: we can prioritize read-only pilot (7/25 start) and parallelize infra prep so cutover risk is minimized. That reduces the chance we'd need an emergency rollback post-signature.

I've sketched the changes on the risk log (see risk_log_v3.pdf). If we go the credit + appendix route, we should: 
- Ask Acme legal to confirm appendix acceptance in writing (email) by 2028-07-09.
- If not confirmed, propose a single-week extension to signature (new close 2028-07-29) while we complete redline.

If Hannah agrees, I'll draft the concession language for Laura's approval. Connor: please confirm implementation resource availability for the pilot and the Aug 5 cutover.

-Rishi
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: MAP: proposed re-prioritization and contingency for close date

Laura —

Looping you in because procurement is asking for a commercial safety net (SLA credit or holdback) and legal is unlikely to accept appendix post-signature. Rishi proposed a 3% credit for the first six months tied to milestones; Connor has to confirm pilot staffing. We need an approval decision on offering that concession — finance will need a crisp concession text and limit.

If we decline to offer credit, the fallback is to agree to shift the signature target to 2028-07-29 (one-week extension) and continue to push the pilot start. I prefer the credit route to preserve the original close date if Laura thinks the margin impact is acceptable.

Thanks,
Hannah

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-07-06T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP: proposed re-prioritization and contingency for close date

Team —

Thanks for the clear options and the risk log. After quick review with finance, we will approve the concession as proposed with the following guardrails: 

- Concession: 3% credit on first six months of billable usage, triggered only if Acme's legal rejects the appendix and blocks full production roll-out within 30 days of signature.
- Concession cap: max $100k.
- Sign-off: Sales to get a written confirmation from Acme legal by 2028-07-09 that appendix is acceptable; if not provided, the concession will be included in the contract and signed by both parties.
- Contingency: If Acme legal wants the clause integrated pre-signature, we accept a one-week shift to signature (new target 2028-07-29) but will require a mutual action plan update and executive notification.

Operational asks: 
- Connor: confirm pilot readiness and resource calendar for 7/25 start by EOD 2028-07-06.
- Rishi: please draft the concession language and an SLA credit triggering rule; include remediation steps and clear measurement points.
- Hannah: request written appendix acceptance from Acme legal by 2028-07-09; if we don't get it, push the signature to 7/29 under the contingency path.

I'll approve the concession in principle; finance is comfortable with the cap and the measurement approach. If anything changes materially, escalate to me immediately.

Laura Bennett
Director, Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

---
Updated MAP summary (post-decision):
- Signature target: 2028-07-22 (preserve), fallback signature: 2028-07-29 (one-week extension)
- Pilot (read-only): start 2028-07-25
- Cutover (prod): 2028-08-05 (soft target)
- Risk acceptance: procurement/legal residency risk accepted with 3% credit cap $100k if appendix rejected
